'''Adam Hisham Hamawy''' ({{Lang|ar|ٱدم هشام حموي}}; born 1969/1970)<ref name="nj">{{cite news |last1=McDougall |first1=AJ |title=A N.J. doctor saved a U.S. senator in Iraq. Now he's running for Congress. |url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2026/01/a-nj-doctor-saved-a-us-senator-in-iraq-now-hes-running-for-congress.html |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[nj.com]] |date=January 16, 2026}}</ref> is an American [[Plastic surgery|plastic surgeon]] and former [[United States Army Medical Corps|U.S. Army physician]].<ref name="USarmy">{{citation|title=Former US Army doctor Adam Hamawy wins Democratic House primary in New Jersey|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/06/03/politics/adam-hamawy-new-jersey-house-democrat|website=CNN|access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref> Hamawy specializes in both cosmetic and [[Reconstructive surgery|reconstructive]] procedures at his practice in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].<ref name=PlasticSurgeon>Multiple sources label Hamawy as a [[Plastic surgery|plastic surgeon]], in which he specializes in both [[Reconstructive surgery|reconstructive]] and cosmetic procedures: 
*{{cite news |last1=McDougall |first1=AJ |title=A N.J. doctor saved a U.S. senator in Iraq. Now he's running for Congress. |url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2026/01/a-nj-doctor-saved-a-us-senator-in-iraq-now-hes-running-for-congress.html |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[nj.com]] |date=January 16, 2026}}
*{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Joey |date=May 11, 2026 |title=After super PAC's ad blitz, Hamawy internal poll puts him in the lead |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/after-super-pacs-ad-blitz-hamawy-internal-poll-puts-him-in-the-lead/ |access-date=May 15, 2026 |website=[[New Jersey Globe]] |language=en-US}}
</ref> He is the Democratic nominee for [[New Jersey's 12th congressional district]] after winning the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 12|2026 Democratic Primary]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 New Jersey US House 12 |url=https://votes.decisiondeskhq.com/races/2026-06-02/new-jersey-us-house-12-democratic-primary |access-date=June 2, 2026 |website=Decision Desk HQ}} {{Dead link|date=November 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

Hamawy gained national attention in 2024 as part of a volunteer team of [[Physicians in the United States|American doctors]] in [[Gaza strip|Gaza]] who were unable to leave after [[Israel]] seized and closed the [[Rafah border crossing]] during the [[Gaza war]]. [[Army National Guard]] veteran and [[U.S. Senator|U.S. senator]] [[Tammy Duckworth]], who credits Hamawy with saving her life when they were both serving in the [[Iraq War]] in 2004, personally intervened to help them leave. Hamawy was one of three doctors who chose to stay behind until the non-Americans on the team could also depart.

In 2026, Hamawy entered [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 12|the Democratic primary]] for [[New Jersey's 12th congressional district]] to succeed Congresswoman [[Bonnie Watson Coleman]] after she announced her retirement. Hamawy won the primary, setting him up as the strong favorite to succeed Watson Coleman in the heavily Democratic district.

==Early life ==
Hamawy was born in [[Egypt]] and moved to [[Old Bridge Township, New Jersey]], with his family when he was a baby.<ref name="politico2026">{{cite news |last1=Friedman |first1=Matt |title=The history of Hamawy and The Blind Sheikh |newspaper=[[Politico]] |date=May 5, 2026 |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/new-jersey-playbook/2026/05/05/the-history-of-hamawy-and-the-blind-sheikh-00906080 |access-date=May 21, 2026 |quote=Hamawy, who was born in Egypt and came to the United States as a baby, was never charged with anything.... Hamawy's campaign pointed out that the initial story was written in FrontPage Magazine, a website affiliated with the anti-Islam David Horowitz Freedom Center, and called it 'guilt-by-association attacks on Muslim and Arab candidates.'}}</ref><ref name="nj" /> Raised in Old Bridge by Egyptian immigrant parents,<ref name="nj"/> he attended [[Rutgers University–New Brunswick]] for his undergraduate studies and [[New Jersey Medical School]] at the [[University of Medicine and Dentistry of New Jersey]] (now at [[Rutgers University–Newark|Rutgers University, Newark]]). He completed his [[Residency (medicine)|medical residency]] in general surgery at [[Weill Cornell Medicine]] and his [[Fellowship (medicine)|fellowship]] in [[plastic surgery]] at [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]].<ref name="practice" /> In 2018, he obtained an [[MBA]] from [[Rutgers University–Camden]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Adam Hamawy |url=https://business.camden.rutgers.edu/2019/05/17/dr-adam-hamawy/ |publisher=[[Rutgers University–Camden|Rutgers University, Camden]] |access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref>

== Medical career ==
===Combat physician===
Hamawy enlisted in the [[New Jersey National Guard]] and served eight years as a [[reconstructive surgeon]], a general surgeon, and a [[flight surgeon]] in the Medical Corps during the [[Iraq War]], including nine months in [[Baghdad]] at the 31st Combat Support Hospital with the [[U.S. Army]].<ref name="nbc" /><ref name="nj" /><ref name="duck">{{cite news |last1=Duckworth |first1=Tammy |title=The Day Tammy Duckworth's Black Hawk Went Down |url=https://www.chicagomag.com/chicago-magazine/april-2021/the-day-tammy-duckworths-black-hawk-went-down/ |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[Chicago Mag]] |date=March 30, 2021}}</ref> One of his patients was future [[U.S. Senator]] [[Tammy Duckworth]], who credited him with helping save her life after her [[Blackhawk helicopter]] was shot down in 2004.<ref name="nj" /> Duckworth has said, "When I was wounded, within 20 minutes, I was in front of him—and he is the doctor who not only saved my life, but was able to prevent me from becoming a triple amputee by employing a vascular procedure that he'd just learned in medical school."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harrington |first1=Adam |last2=O'Keefe |first2=Ed |last3=Cramer |first3=Matthew |title=Doctor who saved Sen. Duckworth's life is now trapped in Gaza |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/doctor-saved-sen-duckworth-trapped-gaza/ |access-date=March 30, 2026 |publisher=[[CBS News]] |date=May 15, 2024}}</ref> The Combat Support Hospital treated an average of 15 traumas a day, but on the busiest days, such as during the [[Second Battle of Fallujah]], they treated up to 40.<ref name="duck" />

When Hamawy separated from the Army he had risen to the rank of [[Lieutenant colonel (United States)|lieutenant colonel]].<ref name="nj2" /><ref name="practice">{{cite web |title=Adam Hamawy, MD, FACS |url=https://samraplasticsurgery.com/adam-hamawy-md-facs/ |publisher=Samra Plastic Surgery |access-date=March 31, 2026}}</ref> He has received a [[Meritorious Service Medal (United States)|Meritorious Service Medal]] and three [[Army Commendation Medal]]s.<ref name="Dr. Adam H. Hamawy at U.S. News">{{cite news |title=Dr. Adam H. Hamawy |url=https://health.usnews.com/doctors/adam-hamawy-654380 |access-date=May 17, 2026 |work=[[U.S. News & World Report]]}}</ref>

=== Private medical practice ===
Since returning from military service, Hamawy has been a plastic surgeon in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].<ref name=PlasticSurgeon/>

Hamawy was cited regarding a plastic surgery mobile game that appeared targeted at children, criticizing the game for its effect on their [[self-esteem]] and [[body dysphoria]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Weinberg |first1=Lindsay |title='Dangerous' Beverly Hills Clinic App May Encourage Kids to Get Plastic Surgery |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/style/kids-plastic-surgery-app-is-dangerous-doctors-say-1106669/ |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=April 27, 2018}}</ref>

== Physician in disaster zones ==
===September 11 attacks===
Hamawy treated the wounded and first responders immediately after the [[September 11 attacks]] while completing his residency at [[NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital]].<ref name="nj2">{{cite news |last1=McDougall |first1=A.J. |title=Sen. Bernie Sanders makes endorsement in crowded NJ-12 race |url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2026/05/sen-bernie-sanders-makes-endorsement-in-crowded-nj-12-race.html |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=[[nj.com]] |date=May 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Brien |first1=Owen |title=Dr. Adam Hamawy speaks on his experiences performing surgeries in the heart of the Gaza Strip |url=https://thewhitonline.com/74146/news/dr-adam-hamawy-speaks-on-his-experiences-performing-surgeries-in-the-heart-of-the-gaza-strip/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=[[The Whit]] |date=October 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Wilkens |first1=Brett |title='Prepared to Fight': Sanders Endorses NJ Medicare for All Advocate Dr. Adam Hamawy for Congress |url=https://www.commondreams.org/news/sanders-endorses-hamawy |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=[[Common Dreams]] |date=May 4, 2026}}</ref>

===Gaza===
In May 2024, Hamawy joined a volunteer international mission organized by the Palestinian-American Medical Association and the [[World Health Organization]]. The original plan was to spend two weeks working as part of a 20-person medical team of physicians at the [[Gaza European Hospital]] in [[Khan Younis]]. While there he performed 120 surgeries, more than half of them on children.<ref name="nj" />

[[Israel]] seized and closed the [[Rafah border crossing]] shortly after his arrival, trapping the physicians in Gaza. The team was unable to leave at the end of its mission, and stayed an additional seven days.<ref name="ap">{{cite news |last1=Deeb |first1=Sarah |title=As Gaza's doctors struggle to save lives, many lose their own in Israeli airstrikes |url=https://apnews.com/article/gaza-war-doctors-hospitals-israel-72e511121502914a76ac9b03030b5c98 |access-date=March 30, 2026 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Abigail |last2=Mitchell |first2=Andrea |title=17 of 20 U.S. doctors stuck in Gaza depart with the help of American officials, source says |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/17-20-us-doctors-stuck-gaza-depart-help-us-officials-source-says-rcna152866 |access-date=March 30, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=May 18, 2026}}</ref> Senator [[Tammy Duckworth]] personally intervened to help 17 of the doctors leave by speaking to [[Israeli Ambassador to the United States]] [[Michael Herzog (ambassador)|Michael Herzog]] and delivering a letter that Hamawy had written to [[U.S. President|President]] [[Joe Biden]].<ref name="politico">{{cite news |last1=Gideon |first1=Joseph |title=Duckworth brings Gaza medical team's pleas directly to White House |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2024/05/19/duckworth-gaza-medical-team-pleas-white-house-00158799 |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[Politico]] |date=May 19, 2024}}</ref><ref name="nbc2">{{cite news |last1=Marquez |first1=Alexandra |title=Sen. Tammy Duckworth endorses House candidate who saved her life in Iraq |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/sen-tammy-duckworth-endorses-house-candidate-saved-life-iraq-rcna254248 |access-date=March 30, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=January 16, 2026}}</ref> Hamawy refused to leave until the other members of the team from Jordan, Egypt, and Australia were also able to leave, saying: "When you go in as a team, you leave as a team. That's the right thing to do, and that's what was bred into us [in the Army]."<ref name="nj" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Bellware |first1=Kim |title=U.S. doctor who refused to leave Gaza says he 'cannot abandon my team' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/05/18/adam-hamawy-gaza-doctor-evacuation/ |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[The Washington Post]] |date=May 18, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Del Rey |first1=Michelle |last2=Garcia |first2=Eric |title=Senator Tammy Duckworth is trying to get doctor who saved her life in Iraq out of Gaza |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/senator-duckworth-gaza-doctor-iraq-b2545781.html |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[The Independent]] |date=May 15, 2024}}</ref>

Hamawy told the ''[[New York Times]]'' after he returned, "Children who lost limbs and could not run or play specifically said they wished they had died, and some wanted to kill themselves."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sidhwa |first1=Feroze |title=65 Doctors, Nurses and Paramedics: What We Saw in Gaza |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/10/09/opinion/gaza-doctor-interviews.html |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 9, 2024}}</ref> In an interview with [[NPR]], he said: "Many of these patients die when they arrive to the hospital. The mortality rate is 80%. In our most recent war in Iraq and Afghanistan, the mortality rate was 10%."<ref name="npr" /> He said this was mainly due to lack of medication, personnel, and adequate resources.<ref name="nj" /> Hamawy said the European Hospital "was a completely benign civilian hospital with no tunnels underneath it".<ref>{{cite news |last1= Hauenstein |first1= Hanno |title= Dr Adam Hamawy: I've Never Seen Devastation Like in Gaza |url=https://jacobin.com/2024/08/hamawy-gaza-israel-devestation-medical |access-date=May 20, 2026 |website=[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]] |date= August 16, 2024}}</ref> The [[Israeli Defense Force]] claimed that Hamas leader [[Muhammed Sinwar]] was killed on May 13, 2025, in a tunnel underneath the hospital.<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Usaid |last1=Siddiqui |first2=Stephen |last2=Quillen |first3=Farah |last3=Najjar |first4=Joseph |last4=Stepansky |title=Israel says it finds Mohammed Sinwar's body in Gaza |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/6/8/live-israel-kills-5-wounds-70-seeking-aid-in-gaza-in-latest-mass-shooting?update=3761137 |access-date=June 8, 2025 |publisher=Al Jazeera English |language=en}}</ref>

[[U.S. Representative]] [[Bonnie Watson Coleman]], who represents Princeton in Congress, said then that she was "deeply relieved" when he returned from Gaza. She later invited him as her guest at President [[Donald Trump]]'s 2025 [[State of the Union]].<ref name="nj" />

In June 2024, Hamawy testified to a congressional briefing to describe his experience treating patients in Gaza.<ref name="npr">{{cite news |last1=Lim |first1=Megan |last2=Justine |first2=Kenin |last3=Shapiro |first3=Ari |title=Surgeon who saved Sen. Duckworth says he couldn't save her with those wounds in Gaza |url=https://www.npr.org/2024/06/26/nx-s1-5020185/surgeon-who-saved-sen-duckworth-says-he-couldnt-save-her-with-those-wounds-in-gaza |access-date=March 30, 2026 |publisher=[[NPR]] |work=[[All Things Considered]] |date=June 26, 2024}}</ref>

===Other disasters===
Hamawy volunteered to provide medical services after the [[siege of Sarajevo]], the [[2010 Haitian earthquake]], and the [[Syrian civil war]].<ref>{{cite news |title=US health workers sound alarm on Gaza medical crisis after returning from war zone |url=https://thearabweekly.com/us-health-workers-sound-alarm-gaza-medical-crisis-after-returning-war-zone |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[Arab Weekly]] |date=June 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Adely |first1=Hannan |title=This NJ doctor helped save Sen. Tammy Duckworth. He's been to Gaza to help at hospitals |url=https://northjersey.com/story/news/2024/10/03/adam-hamawy-princeton-nj-volunteer-in-gaza/74888464007/ |access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[northjersey.com]] |date=October 3, 2024}}</ref>

== 2026 U.S. House of Representatives campaign ==
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 12}}

Hamawy entered [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 12|the Democratic primary]] for [[New Jersey's 12th congressional district]] to succeed [[Bonnie Watson Coleman]] after she announced her retirement. He has been endorsed by U.S. Senators [[Tammy Duckworth]] and [[Bernie Sanders]], U.S. Representatives [[Ro Khanna]] and [[Ilhan Omar]], former Representative [[Jamaal Bowman]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/in-packed-nj-12-race-bernie-sanders-will-support-adam-hamawy/|title=In packed NJ-12 race, Bernie Sanders will support Adam Hamawy|last=Fox|first=Joey|date=May 2, 2026|access-date=May 2, 2026|website=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}</ref><ref name="Hamawyprog">{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidernj.com/dixon-drops-out-backs-hamawy/|title=Dixon Drops out, Backs Hamawy|last=Pizzaro|first=Max|date=April 21, 2026|access-date=April 21, 2026|website=InsiderNJ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/hamawy-endorsed-by-khanna-in-nj-12/|title=Hamawy endorsed by Khanna in NJ-12|last=Fox|first=Joey|date=May 4, 2026|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=New Jersey Globe|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidernj.com/press-release/rep-ilhan-omar-endorses-hamawy-for-nj-12/|title=Rep. Ilhan Omar Endorses Hamawy for NJ-12|date=April 24, 2026|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=InsiderNJ}}</ref> and former [[New Jersey General Assembly]] member [[Sadaf Jaffer]].<ref name="nbc2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/jaffer-endorses-hamawy-in-nj-12/|title=Jaffer endorses Hamawy in NJ-12|last=Fox|first=Joey|date=February 19, 2026|access-date=February 20, 2026|website=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}</ref> Hamawy has also been endorsed by numerous [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] organizations, including the [[Justice Democrats]],<ref name="JusticeDems">{{cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/justice-democrats-add-hamawy-to-2026-slate/|title=Justice Democrats add Hamawy to 2026 slate|first=Joey|last=Fox|date=March 30, 2026|access-date=March 30, 2026|website=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}</ref> [[Our Revolution]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bsky.app/profile/our-revolution.bsky.social/post/3miyxbezpt323|title=We proudly endorse Dr. Adam Hamawy for Congress in NJ-12, a combat trauma surgeon, veteran & lifelong humanitarian.|date=April 8, 2026|access-date=April 8, 2026}}</ref> [[PAL PAC]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/pro-palestinian-pac-intended-to-counter-aipac-endorses-hamawy-in-nj-12/|title=Pro-Palestinian PAC, intended to counter AIPAC, endorses Hamawy in NJ-12|last=Fox|first=Joey|date=March 26, 2026|access-date=March 26, 2026|website=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}</ref> and [[Track AIPAC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/hamawy-endorsed-by-cair-action-for-nj-12/|title=Hamawy endorsed by CAIR Action for NJ-12|last=Fox|date=March 24, 2026|access-date=March 24, 2026|website=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}</ref>

In the first quarter of 2026, Hamawy announced that he had raised nearly $550,000, which the ''[[New Jersey Globe]]'' said would mean he "may be NJ-12's best-funded Democrat".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fox |first1=Joey |title=Hamawy may be NJ-12's best-funded Democrat after nearly $550k 1st quarter |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/hamawy-may-be-nj-12s-best-funded-democrat-after-nearly-550k-1st-quarter/ |access-date=April 11, 2026 |website=[[New Jersey Globe]] |date=April 1, 2026}}</ref>
According to a poll conducted by Workbench Strategy and funded by Hamawy, he was leading a "splintered field".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fox |first1=Joey |title=After super PAC's ad blitz, Hamawy internal poll puts him in the lead |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/after-super-pacs-ad-blitz-hamawy-internal-poll-puts-him-in-the-lead// |access-date=May 20, 2026 |website=[[New Jersey Globe]] |date= May 11, 2026}}</ref>

During the 2026 Democratic primary campaign, Hamawy's 1995 testimony as a defense witness in the trial of [[Omar Abdel-Rahman]] for conspiring to assassinate Egyptian President [[Hosni Mubarak]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Neumeister |first1=Larry |title=Sheik gave no death order, trial told |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-jersey-journal-testimony-in-trial-of/197456592/ |access-date=May 21, 2026 |website=[[The Jersey Journal]] — via the [[Associated Press]] |date=July 26, 1995 | quote=A medical student who was with Sheik Omar Abdel-Rahman when he allegedly told an FBI informant to kill Egypt's president testified yesterday at the sheik's terrorism trial that he never heard such a command. The student, Adam Hishan Hamawy, 26, of Old Bridge, N.J., said he was seated directly behind the sheik during the 13-hour journey in a minivan from Avenel, N.J., to Detroit during Thanksgiving weekend in 1991.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Fried |first1=Joseph P. |title=Defense Witness Says Sheik Never Urged Assassination |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/07/26/nyregion/defense-witness-says-sheik-never-urged-assassination.html |access-date=May 21, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 26, 1995 | quote=Contradicting testimony by the Government's chief informer, a supporter of Sheik Omar Abdel Rahman testified yesterday that the militant Muslim cleric had not urged the informer to murder President Hosni Mubarak of Egypt.... The informer, Emad Salem, testified earlier in the seven-month-old trial that Mr. Abdel Rahman, during a 13-hour drive from New Jersey to Detroit in 1991, urged him to kill Mr. Mubarak. But yesterday's witness, Adam Hisham Hamawy, said that he had sat immediately behind Mr. Abdel Rahman and the informer in the small van and had not heard the cleric make any such statement during the long ride.}}</ref> received media attention after the ''[[Wall Street Journal]]'' published an opinion column by [[Michael Mukasey]], the judge in the case, describing Hamawy's interactions with Abdel-Rahman.<ref name=wSJ>{{cite news |last1=Mukasey |first1=Michael B. |title=The 'Blind Sheikh' and the Candidate |url=https://www.wsj.com/opinion/the-blind-sheikh-and-the-candidate-0a37e742 |access-date=May 21, 2026 |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=May 7, 2026 | quote=Mr. Hamawy appeared before me as a defense witness when I presided at the 1995 trial of Omar Abdel Rahman, also known as the "Blind Sheikh", who was convicted of numerous offenses, including seditious conspiracy against America—providing the spiritual guidance for the first World Trade Center bombing in 1993—and conspiring to assassinate Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak. The defense offered Mr. Hamawy's testimony to rebut a prosecution witness's testimony that, during a trip to Detroit, Abdel Rahman had urged that witness to point a rifle at Mubarak's chest and kill him.}}</ref><ref name=NYT2026>Tully, Tracey. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/30/nyregion/adam-hamawy-election-nj.html "A Candidate’s Past Ties to a Militant Cleric Are Surfacing in a N.J. House Race; Dr. Adam Hamawy, a New Jersey Democrat with big-name support on the left, has touted his humanitarian work, but some opponents want to talk about Sheikh Omar Abdel Rahman."], ''[[The New York Times]]'', May 30, 2026. Accessed June 1, 2026. "Dr. Hamawy has distanced himself from the sheikh on the campaign trail, saying, 'I condemn his violent rhetoric and actions.' When pressed on what had motivated him to travel with Mr. Abdel Rahman as a younger man, Dr. Hamawy downplayed the cleric’s reputation for fiery rhetoric, calling him a 'blind old man' who was dependent on volunteers from the Muslim community to care for him. 'He wasn’t preaching death and destruction all the time,' Dr. Hamawy added. 'He had certain views that he spoke in certain forums, but that’s not what he did every single day.'"</ref> Hamawy was never charged or accused of any wrongdoing, and he characterized the renewed coverage as partisan "guilt-by-association" attacks.<ref name="politico2026" />

[[American Priorities]], a pro-Palestinian political action committee, spent more than $1.5 million on campaign ads that focus on his work as a physician with the U.S. Army, far outspending the other candidates in the race.<ref name=NYT2026/><ref>Stile, Charles. [https://www.northjersey.com/story/opinion/columnists/2026/05/18/adam-hamawy-nj-12-district-opinion/90084461007/ "Will Adam Hamawy's ties to Omar Abdel-Rahman slow his surge? | Opinion"], ''[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]'', May 18, 2026. Accessed May 18, 2026. "But he also enjoys an advantage from American Priorities, a pro-Palestinian political action group that is spending $10 million in races around the country to counter the influence of pro-Israel groups. It has spent $1 million so far on the race, airing cable television and digital ads highlighting Hamawy's career as a military doctor. His competitors haven't come anywhere close to matching that kind of blitz."</ref> The PAC spent $2&nbsp;million supporting Hamawy in the race.<ref>Fox, Joey. [https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/pro-palestine-super-pac-plans-to-spend-2-million-supporting-hamawy/ "Pro-Palestine super PAC plans to spend $2 million supporting Hamawy American Priorities begins $600k ad buy in crowded NJ-12 primary"], ''[[New Jersey Globe]]'', April 24, 2026. Accessed May 18, 2026. "American Priorities PAC, a brand-new but deep-pocketed super PAC intended to support progressive, Israel-skeptical candidates around the country, announced this morning that it is kicking off an enormous investment supporting Adam Hamawy, one of the leading Democratic candidates in the open Central Jersey district. For now, the PAC has announced a $600,000 ad buy that will run for the next two-and-a-half weeks, a sum that's larger than what any individual candidate (including Hamawy) has reported raising for their own campaigns thus far.... With just over a month to go until the June 2 Democratic primary, American Priorities says that it plans to eventually double that ad investment and spend "approximately $2 million" on the 12th district campaign in total."</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=McDougall |first=AJ |date=June 3, 2026 |title=Plastic surgeon beats huge field in hotly contested Democratic primary in N.J.'s 12th District |url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2026/06/plastic-surgeon-beats-huge-field-in-hotly-contested-democratic-primary-in-njs-12th-district.html |access-date=June 6, 2026 |work=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref>

Hamawy won the Democratic primary on June 2, defeating 12 other candidates.<ref name=":0" /> This left him as the favorite to win the general election in the heavily Democratic district.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hamawy wins N.J.-12 Democratic nomination after crowded primary |url=https://www.dailyprincetonian.com/article/2026/06/princeton-news-town-hamawy-wins-democratic-nomination-nj-12 |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=The Princetonian |language=en-US}}</ref>

In September 2026, Hamawy attended a protest ahead of a speech by Israeli prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] at the [[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|United Nations General Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Speri |first=Alice |last2=McMenamin |first2=Lex |date=2026-09-24 |title=Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/24/netanyahu-un-protests |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Hamawy is married, and as of 2025 he lives with his wife and their four children in the [[Monmouth Junction, New Jersey|Monmouth Junction]] section of [[South Brunswick, New Jersey]].<ref name="nbc">{{cite news |last1=Thorp |first1=Frank |last2=Richards |first2=Zoë |last3=Williams |first3=Abigail |title=The doctor who saved Sen. Tammy Duckworth in Iraq is trapped in Gaza. Now she's trying to save him. |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/doctor-saved-tammy-duckworth-iraq-trapped-gaza-adam-hamawy-rcna152291 |access-date=March 30, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=May 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Watson Coleman |first1=Bonnie |title=Live Discussion with Dr. Hamawy in the West Bank |url=https://watsoncoleman.house.gov/newsroom/videos/watch/live-discussion-with-dr-hamawy-in-the-west-bank |publisher=[[Bonnie Watson Coleman]] |access-date=March 30, 2026}}</ref>
